stops.narrative: Trace resources before harvest and repayment later. What would you ask a household before accepting the policy’s promised benefit?
Describe visible royal signs, then use the account of common pottery to identify work the image omits.
Find construction features in the garment. Distinguish them from evidence about rotating service, resettlement and provisioning.

conclusion: Proposals, royal images and finished objects can conceal different parts of work. Add household evidence and distinct voices before judging benefits or choices.

evidence.prompt: Which evidence would best test whether the proposed Song loan helped a particular household?

options.text: The official memorial says the policy would benefit people.
options.feedback: That explains the authors’ justification, not the household’s actual experience.

options.text: Dated local borrowing and repayment records, read alongside that household’s circumstances.
options.feedback: These could test timing, terms, harvest conditions and collection against the promise. Surviving records still need interpretation.

options.text: The Mali map depicts a ruler holding gold.
options.feedback: A foreign royal image cannot establish the outcome of a particular Song loan.
